$comment: EXPERIMENTAL — declarative mapping from the canonical Part IV instance-data model (criterion C31, slc-stand-to-spec-avg) to the UBL QualificationApplicationRESPONSE XML — the ECONOMIC-OPERATOR side. This is the counterpart to part-IV.request.mapping.json (the buyer side). Only the `response` sub-object is mapped here; the buyer's `requirement` maps to the request document. Same engine and `records` construct as Part III: the answer indicators, the relied-upon branch, the turnover period+amount answer, and cross-linked electronic evidence. Property keys use the EDM `responsepath` form (…/R1), the authentic 'XML Path like ID' with schemeID='criterion'.

$notes.amount: The turnover AMOUNT answer uses a `value` body with a data-sourced attribute: cbc:ResponseAmount@currencyID is sourced from the instance (turnover.amount.currency), so the currency roundtrips. This exercises the value-attribute { from } path (BR-TCR-08 numeric datatypes) that Part III did not.
$notes.period: The turnover PERIOD answer uses the generic `object` body: turnover.period {startDate,endDate} -> cac:ApplicablePeriod/{cbc:StartDate,cbc:EndDate} (BR-TCR-08-09), the same construct C01 used for the exclusion period.
$notes.conditionalBranch: fulfilledByItself gates the ONFALSE relied-upon branch. reliedUpon (and the relied-upon entity) are separate records; when the EO fulfils by itself they are simply absent from the instance data and emit nothing.
$notes.evidence: Same explicit cross-link as Part III: evidence[].id -> cac:Evidence/cbc:ID, and the EVIDENCE_IDENTIFIER record's `references` emits one cac:EvidenceSupplied/cbc:ID per entry valued by that same id (BR-TCR-09).

rules.$comment: C31 criterion declaration — criterion UUID (from the EA export). Pure constant metadata: no instance-data home, not written back on import.
Economic-operator answer records. Each `entries` item emits one cac:TenderingCriterionResponse with a keyed property id (…/R1) and one body branch.

entries.$comment: RG1/RSG1/QSG1/Q1 — 'Does the EO fulfil the criteria by itself?' (INDICATOR).
RG1/RSG1/QSG1/QSG1/Q1 — 'In the case of no – Relied upon or not' (INDICATOR). ONFALSE branch; present only when the EO does not fulfil by itself.
RG1/RSG1/QSG1/QSG1/QSG1/Q1 — 'Name of the entity' (DESCRIPTION). ONTRUE under relied-upon.
RG1/RSG1/QSG1/QSG1/QSG1/Q2 — 'ID of the entity' (ECONOMIC_OPERATOR_IDENTIFIER). Emitted as a plain response identifier value.
RG1/RSG1/QSG2/Q1 — 'Start date; End date' (PERIOD, BR-TCR-08-09). Generic `object` body: turnover.period -> cac:ApplicablePeriod.
RG1/RSG1/QSG2/Q2 — 'Amount' (AMOUNT, BR-TCR-08). Value with a data-sourced currencyID attribute so the currency roundtrips.
RG1/RSG1/QSG2/QSG1/Q1 — 'Is this information available electronically?' for the turnover figure (INDICATOR).

RG1/RSG1/QSG2/QSG1/QSG1/Q1 — turnover 'Evidence Supplied' (EVIDENCE_IDENTIFIER, 1..n). `references`: one cac:EvidenceSupplied/cbc:ID per evidence entry, valued by that entry's `id`. Links to the cac:Evidence records below (BR-TCR-09).
RG1/RSG1/QSG3/Q1 — 'date the EO was set up or started trading' (DATE). Fallback when turnover is not available for the whole period.
RG1/RSG1/QSG3/QSG1/Q1 — 'Is this information available electronically?' for the start-trading date (INDICATOR).
RG1/RSG1/QSG4/Q1 — criterion-level 'Is this information available electronically?' (INDICATOR).

rules.$comment: Turnover evidence documents (QSG2) -> cac:Evidence. One record per evidence entry; referenced by the QSG2/QSG1/QSG1/Q1 record above via shared ids. `importVia: references` — on import these are reconstructed per-block by that record's `references.resolve` (all three evidence sets share this one wrapper), so this rule is export-only.
Start-trading evidence documents (QSG3) -> cac:Evidence. Export-only (see importVia note on the QSG2 evidence rule).

Criterion-level evidence documents (QSG4) -> cac:Evidence. All three evidence sets share the one document-level cac:Evidence list, each entry keyed by its own unique id. Export-only (see importVia note on the QSG2 evidence rule).
